evidenceLimits: Every method body in Modules-ASM is an interop wrapper ending in IL2CPP.il2cpp_runtime_invoke; no C# source for a native body is reachable from these assemblies. The bodies quoted below come from the wpnovr disassembly of GameAssembly.dll, not from the interop assembly.

Nothing here is game-verified: no game process was started and no r2modman profile was written. The clone a request performs is built with the game's own allocator and constructor, which no static read can confirm at runtime; that check is recorded under unverified.
RVAs are valid for GameAssembly.dll sha256 C6A5C3CD...D7BF55 only.

nativeWritePoints.meaning: The shot gate. Zeroing it lets the next shot happen on the next frame; nothing in the decoded code reads it as a duration or derives anything else from its value.
nativeWritePoints.readSite: Gear.BulletWeaponArchetype.Update 0x145C950 writes it at 0x145D2DB (m_nextShotTimer = now + ShotDelay)

notWritten.reason: No decoded read site consumes it in this build (the wpnovr reverse scan over the per-shot path found none), so zeroing it would be a write with no observable effect. It is left alone rather than written for symmetry.

rows.gap: missing native archetype rebuild entry point: FireMode selects which archetype class SetupArchetype constructs, and an instance already holds the class it was built as, so only a rebuild (which replaces the instance's timer state) could change it

nativeFacts.meaning: Semi=0, Burst=1, Auto=2, SemiBurst=3 (SentryGun*=10..13). The shipped code switches on it while building the archetype, not while firing.
nativeFacts.readSite: Gear.BulletWeapon.SetupArchetype 0x1462050 at 0x146214B (mov eax,[rax+60h] / sub eax,1 / je) selecting BWA_Auto / BWA_Burst / BWA_Semi / BWA_SemiBurst

nativeFacts.meaning: The frame path also reads FireMode (0x145CB94 cmp dword ptr [rax+60h],1) for the burst-continuation branch, so a changed block field does reach this branch — but the archetype's own class, its m_burstMax and its burst counters are what decide how a shot sequence actually runs. A block write alone therefore produces a weapon whose data says one mode and whose class advances another.
The burst length is copied out of the block only here, from BurstShotCount (0xCC) into m_burstMax (0x60); nothing on the per-shot path re-reads it for these classes.
nativeFacts.consequence: The burst_count field this vocabulary carries is writeable on a burst archetype (both copies are refreshed by the applier) and refused with override-field-unknown on an archetype that has no such field at all.

nativeFacts.meaning: No decoded member of the weapon or archetype carries a press-versus-release trigger policy; what the block holds is m_triggerNeedsPress's input to the archetype, and no catalog-named mechanism sets it. The row's second required structural parameter therefore has no native destination either.
nativeFacts.derivation: absence in the decoded read/write sets and in dump.cs's ArchetypeDataBlock property list

netcodeBoundary.rule: The instance a request lands on is the holder client's own weapon: rate of fire, spread and the burst path are simulated where the weapon is wielded, and a client that never applies the same block still throttles replicated fire events with its own ShotDelay (Gear.BulletWeaponSynced.UpdateRegular 0x145E5B0 at 0x145E689).
netcodeBoundary.consequence: The host decides and the holder's client writes; a machine with no holder client (bot or offline) writes locally. The command channel that carries a request to a client that is not the host is a framework capability this slice does not build, and the applier is written as the body on whichever machine receives it.

whatTheWriteSetDoesNotDo: It never writes the shared GameData blocks. The clone is taken with the game's own constructor, which neither registers the block in a static table nor marks it dirty (GameData.ArchetypeDataBlock..ctor 0x1420060 decoded in full, 54 instructions, no static access), so a clone changes nothing for any other instance.
It never touches the gear pool or the loadout: narrowing which gear a slot offers happens before an instance exists, and this slice reads no pool array and writes none.

It does not re-create the archetype instance. Constructing a replacement is possible, but it discards the burst counters and the charge timer the instance is holding (BWA_Burst.m_burstCurrentCount 0x64, BWA_SemiBurst.m_semiBurstCurrentCount 0x64), which is why the applier keeps the instance and replaces the block it points at.

It writes only the minimum of each MinMaxValue range and copies the maximum as it found it: the shipped recoil path reads Min only (see the read sites above), so writing a maximum would be writing a value nothing consumes.
unverified: The clone is built at runtime through il2cpp_object_new plus an invoke of the class's own parameterless constructor. The constructor's body and the allocation path are decoded, but no static read proves the interop call reaches it in a live process.

The identity of the vtable member at +0x520 that BulletWeapon.Update and Weapon.ApplyRecoil fetch a RecoilDataBlock through is unresolved in wpnovr; both paths end in the same block type and the read/write sets here do not depend on which member it is.

Whether checkpoint restore or gear regeneration rebuilds an archetype outside the OnGearSpawnComplete chain was not settled statically (the reverse scan resolves literal calls only). The replay hook is on OnGearSpawnComplete, the one chain that was decoded.
Whether an unapplied block swap produces a visible divergence between clients, and whether the crosshair consumes the block per frame, need a running game.
inGameVerification: Log a wielded bullet weapon's ArchetypeDataBlock.ShotDelay and m_archeType.m_archetypeData pointer, fire a magazine, and confirm the observed interval matches before any swap.
Apply a fire_rate override and read back m_archetypeData (must be the clone) and m_recoilData (must be non-null); fire again and confirm the interval changed.
Apply a recoil override and confirm the camera kick and crosshair pop change with it.
Wield/unwield, reload and force a gear respawn: the swap must survive the first three and be replayed by the fourth.
Apply the same override on both clients and confirm no visible divergence in the replicated fire rate.
Apply burst_count on a burst weapon and read back m_burstMax and BulletWeapon.m_burstMax; apply a smaller default clip while the magazine is full and read back BulletWeapon.m_clip.
